title: State of NCT of Delhi v. Aftab Ameen Poonawala (Shraddha Walkar Dismemberment)
crime_type: Domestic Homicide / Anatomical Dismemberment / Forest Bone Disposal
court_or_authority: Saket District & Sessions Court, New Delhi / High Court of Delhi
legal_citation: Sessions Case No. 89/2023; FIR No. 659/2022 Mehrauli PS
source: Delhi Police Forensic Crime Branch & Indian Kanoon
ipc_sections: Section 201 IPC (Causing disappearance of evidence of offence)
location: Mehrauli, New Delhi & Vasai, Maharashtra, India
evidence: Recovery of 13 decomposed human bone fragments from Mehrauli forest reserve whose mitochondrial DNA matched victim father
Purchase receipts and digital payment logs for a 300-litre domestic deep-freezer and saw blades immediately post-homicide
Google search history records on suspect phone researching human anatomy, blood-cleaning chemicals, and forensic masking techniques
Blood splatter detected behind refrigerator tiles using luminol chemical spray despite repeated bleach scrubbings
modus_operandi: Strangled live-in partner during domestic argument. Dragged body into bathroom, purchased a 300-litre refrigerator and miniature bone saws. Methodically dismembered corpse into 35 pieces over several days, preserving flesh in deep freezer. Disposed of body parts incrementally in forested areas of South Delhi during 2:00 AM nocturnal walks over several months.
personality_disorder: Antisocial personality structure, cold methodical dissociation, and forensic counter-investigative calculation.
common_traits: Domestic strangulation followed by cold-storage preservation
Methodical anatomical dismemberment with small hand saws
Nocturnal forest dispersion of human remains
Digital search queries researching chemical cleanup of blood
summary: High-profile forensic investigation demonstrating advanced mitochondrial DNA extraction from weathered bone fragments and luminol chemical detection, revolutionizing protocols for domestic dismemberment forensics in India.
